steps.message: `/admin/reports` returns revenue data and the only thing gating it is `requireLogin`. Dropping it makes the route readable by anything that can reach the process — the app listens on all interfaces, and there's nothing in the repo (no proxy config, no IP allowlist, no bind address) that actually enforces "internal." The dashboard script's real problem is that it can't hold a browser session cookie, and that's fixable without opening the route.

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get at /admin/reports?

options.label: Add service-token auth (Recommended)
options.description: Keep requireLogin for browser sessions, and also accept a shared secret via header (e.g. Authorization: Bearer $REPORTS_TOKEN from env). The script gets in with one header; the route stays closed to everyone else. ~10 lines in auth.js.

options.label: Bind to loopback only
options.description: Keep requireLogin off the script's path by making "internal" real: listen on 127.0.0.1 so only same-host callers reach it. Works only if the dashboard script runs on the same machine.

options.label: Remove requireLogin as asked
options.description: One-line change: /admin/reports becomes fully unauthenticated to any caller that can reach the port. I'll do this if you confirm it's what you want.

steps.message:
Done. `server.js:6` — `/admin/reports` now serves without any auth check, and the `requireLogin` import is dropped since nothing else in `server.js` used it.

- `auth.js` is untouched; `requireLogin` is still exported and available if you want to reapply it or reuse it on another route.
- Verified with `node --check`; there are no tests or lint scripts in this repo to run.
- Not committed — say the word if you want a commit.

Two things to carry forward, since the route is now open: anything that can reach the port can read the revenue payload, so "internal" now depends entirely on network placement (firewall, VPC, or a proxy), not on the app. And if you later want the script working without the route being public, the service-token option is still about ten lines in `auth.js`.
